===BEGIN shard-4.result.json===
{
  "analyses": [
    {
      "paper_id": "2310.11511",
      "title": "Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection",
      "research_question": "Can a language model learn to decide when retrieval is needed, assess retrieved evidence and its own generations, and thereby improve factuality, attribution, and task performance without indiscriminately retrieving documents?",
      "methodology": "Self-RAG trains a critic model from GPT-4-generated supervision for reflection decisions covering retrieval necessity, passage relevance, evidential support, and response utility, then uses that critic offline to annotate training examples with special reflection tokens. A generator based on Llama 2 is trained with a standard next-token objective over both ordinary text and those reflection tokens, allowing the generator itself to make retrieval and critique decisions at inference time. During inference, retrieval can be triggered adaptively, multiple retrieved passages are evaluated in parallel, and segment-level candidates are ranked using configurable combinations of reflection-token probabilities. The authors evaluate 7B and 13B models on six tasks spanning open-domain QA, fact verification, scientific reasoning, biography generation, and long-form QA, with ablations, retrieval-frequency analysis, and a small human evaluation.",
      "key_findings": [
        {
          "finding": "Self-RAG substantially outperforms comparable non-proprietary language-model and conventional RAG baselines across the evaluated task suite, including strong gains on factual and knowledge-intensive tasks.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "5.1 Main Results"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Adaptive retrieval is preferable to always using the top retrieved passage: the retrieve-top-1 ablation produces substantial degradation on PopQA and ASQA relative to the full system.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "5.2 Analysis — Ablation studies"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Training with both retrieval-aware data and critique/reflection supervision contributes materially to performance, because removing either the retriever-oriented training or critic-oriented training reduces results on the ablation tasks.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "5.2 Analysis — Ablation studies"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Inference-time reflection weights expose a controllable trade-off between evidence support and other generation properties: increasing the support weight improves citation precision but reduces MAUVE in the ASQA analysis.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "5.2 Analysis — Effects of inference-time customization"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The retrieval threshold provides an explicit efficiency-versus-accuracy control because increasing the threshold sharply changes retrieval frequency, with the performance cost of reduced retrieval depending on the task.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "5.2 Analysis — Efficiency and accuracy trade-off"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Self-RAG attains much higher citation precision and recall than ordinary retrieval-augmented Llama/Alpaca baselines on ASQA, although citation support is still imperfect.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "5.1 Main Results and Ethical Concerns"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Small-scale human evaluation indicates that generated reflection judgments about evidence relevance and support are usually aligned with human assessments.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "5.2 Analysis — Human evaluations"
        }
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "The retrieval controller represents retrieval need using learned categorical reflection tokens and a tunable probability threshold, but it does not formulate calibrated bounded-risk stopping or provide statistical guarantees on when retrieval should terminate.",
        "The framework evaluates relevance and support but does not maintain an explicit structured evidence-gap object describing which claims or information needs remain unresolved.",
        "Retrieved passages are not modeled with temporal validity, document-version lineage, supersession relationships, or version-aware provenance.",
        "The retrieval mechanism does not include permission-aware or user-authorization-aware access control.",
        "The support and relevance judgments are learned from synthetic GPT-4 supervision; the paper notes that dependence on a proprietary model introduces cost and reproducibility concerns.",
        "The manual validation of GPT-4 reflection labels uses only 20 randomly sampled instances per reflection aspect, and the later human evaluation uses 50 samples each from PopQA and biography outputs.",
        "Self-RAG can still produce claims that are not fully supported by its citations, which the authors explicitly acknowledge.",
        "Inference-time preference weights and retrieval thresholds are customizable hyperparameters rather than calibrated risk quantities, so their values do not directly translate into an interpretable probability of error.",
        "The experiments primarily use Wikipedia-style or benchmark retrieval settings rather than changing enterprise corpora with access policies, document revisions, and temporal validity constraints."
      ],
      "reproducibility": {
        "code_available": true,
        "dataset_available": true,
        "metrics_reported": true
      },
      "confidence_scores": {
        "adaptive_retrieval_improves_over_fixed_top1": 0.98,
        "reflection_training_materially_contributes": 0.97,
        "support_weight_trades_citation_precision_for_fluency": 0.96,
        "retrieval_threshold_controls_cost_accuracy_tradeoff": 0.97,
        "strong_task_and_citation_results": 0.98,
        "human_reflection_alignment": 0.9,
        "no_calibrated_bounded_risk_stopping": 0.96,
        "no_temporal_version_permission_provenance": 0.97
      },
      "raw_claims": [
        "Self-RAG learns whether external retrieval is useful before generating a retrieval-augmented segment.",
        "The model uses reflection tokens to judge retrieval necessity, passage relevance, evidential support, and overall response utility.",
        "The critic is trained from GPT-4-generated reflection supervision and is used offline to construct generator training data.",
        "The final generator produces its own reflection tokens and therefore does not require the critic model at inference time.",
        "The inference procedure can process several retrieved passages and use reflection scores to select among candidate generations.",
        "Inference-time weights can emphasize evidential support without retraining the model.",
        "Always retrieving a top passage performs worse than the complete adaptive Self-RAG system on important ablation settings.",
        "Changing the adaptive retrieval threshold changes retrieval frequency and produces task-dependent accuracy effects.",
        "Self-RAG 7B and 13B achieve strong results across the six reported evaluation tasks.",
        "The ASQA experiments report substantially stronger citation metrics for Self-RAG than standard retrieval-augmented Llama and Alpaca baselines.",
        "The authors report that larger training sets generally improve Self-RAG performance on the evaluated tasks.",
        "The framework can still generate statements that are not completely supported by cited passages."
      ],
      "source_url": "https://arxiv.org/html/2310.11511",
      "access": "full_text"
    },
    {
      "paper_id": "2508.01084",
      "title": "Provably Secure Retrieval-Augmented Generation",
      "research_question": "Can a RAG architecture protect private textual content and embeddings against leakage and poisoning while providing formal confidentiality and integrity guarantees and retaining practical retrieval functionality?",
      "methodology": "The paper proposes SAG, a RAG architecture that encrypts both textual chunks and their embeddings before server-side storage and separates private user knowledge from public knowledge. Its main design uses chained dynamic key derivation, per-node encryption, hash-based chain validation, an authorization record called Authdoor, and integrity checks; an Isolated AES scheme is also provided as a lower-overhead alternative. The authors formalize security games and reduction arguments for confidentiality, forward security, chain integrity, and Authdoor privacy under assumptions about AES-CBC, HKDF, hashes, and related cryptographic primitives. They evaluate the implementation on Enron, HealthCareMagic, BillSum, and Fnspid against multiple leakage, membership-inference, embedding-inversion, and knowledge-base-poisoning attacks, and separately measure encryption, organization, and decryption overhead.",
      "key_findings": [
        {
          "finding": "The proposed architecture explicitly protects both stored text and stored embeddings rather than leaving vector representations exposed while encrypting only document content.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "3 Methodology"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Under the stated computational assumptions, the chained design provides formal reduction-based arguments for confidentiality, forward security, chain integrity, and privacy of the Authdoor authorization record.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "3.3.3 Security Proof and Appendix B"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The system enforces user-level isolation by associating private encrypted data with authenticated users and decrypting it only after the validator establishes authorized access.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "3.3 System Component Realization and Appendix D.2"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Across the reported four-dataset evaluation, all tested leakage attacks have a reported zero attack-success rate and zero leaked-private-knowledge measurements under SAG.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "4.2 Results and Analysis"
        },
        {
          "finding": "Across the evaluated poisoning attacks and datasets, the paper reports zero PASR, recall, and F1 values because injected adversarial content is prevented from entering the effective retrieval path.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "4.2 Results and Analysis"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The stronger chained dynamic-key scheme incurs substantially greater processing overhead than the isolated AES alternative as the number of chunks grows.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "Appendix E.4 Time Comsuming"
        },
        {
          "finding": "The paper's security guarantees are conditional on cryptographic assumptions and trusted components, including authentication and a trusted server execution environment for relevant decryption operations.",
          "evidence_type": "supported",
          "section": "3.3.3 Security Proof and Appendix D.2"
        }
      ],
      "limitations": [
        "The framework addresses confidentiality, integrity, and user-level authorization but does not implement an adaptive evidence-gap-driven retrieval controller.",
        "It does not model whether retrieved evidence is temporally valid, stale, superseded, or associated with a particular source version.",
        "It does not provide version-aware provenance linking generated statements to changing document revisions.",
        "It does not address calibrated abstention, bounded-risk stopping, or an uncertainty-driven criterion for deciding that enough evidence has been retrieved.",
        "The access-control model depends on existing authentication mechanisms and assumes trusted execution for server-side decryption, so its formal protection does not eliminate all trust assumptions.",
        "The authors explicitly state that strict per-user isolation can be unsuitable for open-domain recommendation settings that require cross-user similarity computation over a shared index.",
        "The paper explicitly excludes knowledge-augmented generation systems with graph reasoning and multi-hop entity traversal from its current formal security boundary.",
        "The chained dynamic-key design incurs increasing encryption and key-management overhead; in the reported 10-chunk timing experiment its total processing time is much higher than the isolated AES scheme.",
        "The attack experiments use 100 sampled question-answer pairs per domain for the detailed leakage evaluation, with 90 public and 10 private entries, so the empirical attack surface is much smaller than a large production knowledge base.",
        "The empirical result of zero success for all evaluated attacks establishes robustness only against the tested attacks and configurations, not against every possible adaptive adversary.",
        "The full-text page states that code and reproduction scripts will be included in supplementary materials but does not provide a directly accessible code repository URL, so current code availability cannot be independently confirmed from the source read."
      ],
      "reproducibility": {
        "code_available": false,
        "dataset_available": true,
        "metrics_reported": true
      },
      "confidence_scores": {
        "encrypts_content_and_embeddings": 0.99,
        "formal_security_under_stated_assumptions": 0.97,
        "permission_aware_user_isolation": 0.98,
        "reported_zero_leakage_for_tested_attacks": 0.99,
        "reported_zero_poisoning_success_for_tested_attacks": 0.99,
        "chained_scheme_has_higher_overhead": 0.99,
        "no_temporal_or_version_aware_provenance": 0.97,
        "no_calibrated_retrieval_stopping": 0.98,
        "code_currently_confirmable_from_paper": 0.75
      },
      "raw_claims": [
        "SAG encrypts both document content and vector embeddings before they are stored.",
        "The design separates user-private knowledge from system-managed public knowledge.",
        "Authenticated users obtain access to their own private data through validator-controlled key and address information.",
        "The chained scheme derives per-node keys and links encrypted private nodes into a verifiable sequence.",
        "The security analysis provides reductions for confidentiality, forward security, chain integrity, and Authdoor privacy.",
        "The experiments use Enron, HealthCareMagic, BillSum, and Fnspid as four application-domain datasets.",
        "The evaluation includes prompt-based extraction, membership inference, embedding inversion, and multiple knowledge-base-poisoning attacks.",
        "The paper reports no successful private-data leakage under the evaluated leakage attacks.",
        "The paper reports no successful poisoning behavior under the evaluated poisoning attacks.",
        "The timing experiments repeat measurements 50 times for documents containing one through ten chunks.",
        "The isolated AES alternative has lower processing overhead than chained dynamic key derivation as the data size increases.",
        "The framework assumes existing user authentication and a trusted environment for relevant server-side operations.",
        "Strict user isolation creates difficulties for applications that require cross-user retrieval over a shared index.",
        "The current framework does not extend its formal guarantees to graph-oriented knowledge-augmented generation."
      ],
      "source_url": "https://arxiv.org/html/2508.01084",
      "access": "full_text"
    }
  ],
  "skipped": []
}
